insights.insight: 12,302 cryptographically verified receipts spanning physical retail, dining, fuel, warehouse, and SaaS subscriptions represent confirmed purchase events — not inferred intent. At $990K in verified GMV, this is a cookieless signal set built on transaction fact, not behavioral probability.

The protocol sits $9,485 from $1M in verified GMV, with recent 4-hour cycle inflows reaching $5,016 — meaning the crossing arrives on the next material burst, not a trend. For marketers evaluating the network, this is an inflection point for case study and attribution benchmarking.

insights.topic: Velocity deceleration is real but not a collapse
insights.insight: Token velocity dropped from 1.241x on April 12 to 0.819x on April 17 — the steepest single-cycle decline recorded — but acceleration holds at 1.004x, meaning the contraction rate is not yet compounding. The primary mechanical cause is high-volume April 8–12 receipts rolling out of the 7-day window, not a demand reversal.

Active CBSAs expanded to 25 metros in a single heartbeat on April 13, with simultaneous entry from rural Ohio, California, Idaho, Nebraska, and Iowa — followed by Maine and Rhode Island non-metro. For CPG and QSR brands with national footprints, this signals verified purchase data is no longer confined to top-tier urban markets.

insights.topic: SaaS subscriptions as a new verified category
insights.insight: Digital SaaS subscriptions entered the receipt network on April 9 — the first non-physical commerce category in the protocol's history. Brand marketers can now cross-reference physical purchase behavior with software subscription signals, opening a path to verified B2SMB and prosumer audience segments.

A total endpoint blackout on April 14 — 0 of 16 endpoints available — resolved within roughly 12 hours, with 15 metros active and 3 new CBSAs added in the recovery cycle. For brands considering this as infrastructure for always-on attribution, the blackout-and-recovery sequence is the first real stress test of operational durability.
